questions.text: In a typical week, how many times do you do at least 30 minutes of intentional exercise (any type)?
questions.source: IPAQ-SF; OMICS activity items; WHO PA guidelines 2020

questions.text: How many minutes per week do you do vigorous-intensity activity (hard breathing, can only say a few words — e.g. running, fast cycling, HIIT)?
questions.source: IPAQ-SF; WHO PA guidelines 2020; Kodama 2009 meta-analysis (VO2max & CVD)

questions.text: How many minutes per week do you do moderate-intensity activity (noticeably elevated breathing, can hold a conversation — e.g. brisk walking, cycling, swimming at leisure)?
questions.source: IPAQ-SF; WHO PA guidelines 2020

questions.text: On a typical day, how many minutes do you spend walking (including walking to/from transport, errands, leisure)?
questions.source: IPAQ-SF; Paluch 2022 (steps/day & mortality); OMICS activity items

questions.text: How many steps per day do you typically take (including a wearable or phone estimate if you have one)?
questions.source: Paluch 2022 Lancet (steps-mortality); OMICS activity items

questions.text: On a typical weekday, how many hours do you spend sitting or reclining (excluding sleep)?
questions.source: IPAQ-SF; Biswas 2015 (sitting time & mortality); OMICS activity items

questions.text: On a typical day, how many hours do you spend watching TV or streaming video?
questions.source: Katzmarzyk 2009 (TV hours & CVD mortality); OMICS activity items

questions.text: How many days per week do you do muscle-strengthening activities (resistance training, bodyweight exercises, heavy gardening/lifting)?
questions.source: WHO PA guidelines 2020; Stamatakis 2022 (muscle-strengthening & longevity)

questions.text: How would you rate your own cardiovascular fitness compared to others your age?

responses.label: Excellent — I can sustain hard effort for long periods
Below average — get breathless with moderate effort
Poor — breathless with light activity or at rest

triggers.if_response: Poor — breathless with light activity or at rest

questions.source: OMICS activity items; self-rated fitness predicts VO2max (Myers 2017)

questions.text: When you climb 2–3 flights of stairs at a normal pace, how do you feel?
questions.source: OMICS activity items; stair-climb test as VO2max proxy (Petersen 2020); NOTE: betablocker attenuates HR response — perceived breathlessness more reliable than HR in this persona

questions.text: Can you walk at least 1 km (about 10–15 minutes) on flat ground without stopping due to breathlessness, pain, or fatigue?

responses.label: No — I need to stop or can only do shorter distances

questions.source: 6MWT functional capacity assessment; OMICS activity items

questions.text: After vigorous exercise (e.g., running, fast cycling), how quickly does your heart rate feel like it returns to normal?

responses.label: Very slow or I never push hard enough to test

questions.source: Cole 1999 NEJM (HRR & mortality); OMICS activity items; NOTE: betablocker blunts HR and HR recovery — perceived recovery is confounded; cross-reference wearable.hr_recovery if available

questions.text: After a typical workout, how do you feel 24–48 hours later?
questions.source: OMICS activity items; Twist 2012 (DOMS & recovery fitness marker)

questions.text: Do you regularly participate in organized sport or group fitness activities (team sports, classes, running clubs, etc.)?

responses.label: No — I exercise only alone or not at all

questions.source: Oja 2017 (sport participation & longevity); OMICS activity items

questions.text: Does a fitness tracker or smartwatch give you an estimated VO2 max or fitness score? If so, what does it show?

responses.label: No tracker or no VO2max reading

questions.source: Kodama 2009 (VO2max & CVD/mortality); NOTE: betablocker reduces maxHR → wearable VO2max underestimated; flag gap if betablocker persona detected

questions.text: At what level of activity do you typically become breathless or need to slow down?

responses.label: During sustained moderate effort (jogging, fast cycling)
During brisk walking or light housework
During slow walking or dressing / bathing

questions.source: OMICS activity items; MRC dyspnea scale; NOTE: betablocker blunts HR — breathlessness timing is confounded; wearable.hr_recovery preferred for objective confirmation

questions.text: How do you rate your muscular strength and ability to carry out tasks needing physical force (lifting, carrying, getting up from a chair)?

responses.label: Significant weakness — difficulty with everyday tasks

questions.source: OMICS activity items; Ruiz 2008 (grip strength & CVD mortality)

questions.text: Have you ever had your grip strength measured (dynamometer) or completed a formal fitness test? If so, what was the result?

responses.label: Yes — above average or strong for my age
Yes — below average or weak for my age

questions.source: Ruiz 2008 (grip strength & all-cause mortality); Leong 2015 PURE

questions.text: Over the past 12 months, has your overall fitness and ability to do physical tasks changed?
questions.source: OMICS activity items; deconditioning trajectory as independent predictor

questions.text: How would you rate the quality of your sleep for physical recovery (feeling restored and ready to be active the next day)?

responses.label: Excellent — I wake feeling fully recovered
Fair — sometimes wake tired or sore
Poor — rarely feel recovered after sleep

questions.source: OMICS activity items; Simpson 2017 (sleep & muscle recovery); cross-pillar SLP/FIT

questions.text: When you have a long sitting session (e.g., at a desk or in a vehicle), how often do you get up and move?

responses.label: Rarely or never — sit for hours uninterrupted

questions.source: Dunstan 2012 (breaks in sitting & glycemia); Diaz 2017 (sedentary bout duration)

questions.text: Which best describes your typical activity pattern over recent years?

responses.label: Active for several years, recent dip

questions.source: Lee 2012 (lifetime PA & longevity); Wen 2011 (dose-response PA & mortality)

questions.text: How does your self-assessed fitness compare with what objective data (wearable, fitness test) actually shows?

responses.label: I have objective data and it confirms I am fit
I have no objective data — going on feel
Data suggests I am less fit than I thought
Data confirms I am less fit than my peers

questions.source: Perceived-vs-actual fitness gap (PureScore core concept, Doc 18); self-rated fitness vs measured VO2max correlation

questions.text: Has a physical injury, chronic pain, or disability significantly limited your ability to exercise in the past 6 months?

responses.label: Yes — minor limitation, still somewhat active

questions.source: OMICS activity items; injury/pain as primary inactivity mediator

questions.text: Outside of planned exercise, how active is your typical day (e.g., housework, gardening, manual tasks, taking the stairs)?

responses.label: Very active — on my feet most of the day
Moderately active — mix of sitting and moving
Mostly sedentary with brief movement bouts
Almost entirely sedentary outside planned exercise

questions.source: Levine 2014 (NEAT & energy balance); IPAQ-SF; OMICS activity items
